key_headlines.title: Middle East War Fuels Inflation Concerns and Consumption Slowdown
key_headlines.summary: Oil prices are nearing $110, pushing gasoline to 1,900 won per liter and naphtha prices to double, intensifying inflationary pressures and raising fears of a consumption slowdown in South Korea. The government is considering a supplementary budget and deregulation to alleviate supply chain bottlenecks.

key_headlines.title: Government Prioritizes Raw Material Supply for Essential Medical Items Amid Supply Chain Instability
key_headlines.summary: Amid surging oil prices and exchange rates, the government plans to prioritize the supply of raw materials for critical medical necessities like surgical gowns and waste bags. This measure aims to prevent production disruptions caused by instability in petrochemical raw material supply due to the Middle East conflict.

key_headlines.title: Family Business Succession Tax Deduction to Be Significantly Narrowed
key_headlines.summary: South Korea will drastically reduce the scope of the family business succession tax deduction, excluding industries deemed lacking core know-how, such as bakeries that do not bake their own bread. This revision also includes reducing land deductions and introducing pro-rata allocation for concurrent businesses to curb tax loopholes.

key_headlines.title: National Debt Surpasses 1,300 Trillion Won for First Time, Per Capita Debt Rises
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's national debt reached an unprecedented 1,304.5 trillion won in 2025, increasing by 129.4 trillion won in a year, which translates to an average debt of 25.5 million won per citizen. This marks a significant 2.8 million won increase in per capita debt within one year.

key_headlines.title: K-Beauty Industry Faces 'Naphtha Emergency' Due to Supply Chain Disruptions
key_headlines.summary: The K-beauty sector is grappling with a 'Naphtha Emergency' as the prolonged Middle East conflict disrupts supply chains, leading to shortages of essential packaging materials and a 15% hike in raw material costs. Smaller and newer companies are particularly vulnerable, with ODM firms warning of inevitable price adjustments if the situation persists.

sections.Hot Economy News: The Middle East conflict is causing significant inflationary pressure in South Korea, with oil prices approaching $110 and gasoline topping 1,900 won per liter, alongside a doubling of naphtha prices impacting various industries. This situation raises concerns about a potential slowdown in consumer spending. The government plans to address supply chain bottlenecks through a supplementary budget and deregulation, while also prioritizing the supply of raw materials for essential medical items like surgical gowns. Additionally, the national debt has surpassed 1,300 trillion won for the first time, and the K-beauty industry is facing a 'naphtha emergency' due to packaging material shortages. The government is also narrowing the scope of family business succession tax deductions to exclude businesses lacking core know-how.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: South Korea's national debt reached an unprecedented 1,304.5 trillion won in 2025, an increase of 129.4 trillion won in a year, now representing 49% of GDP. This surge is attributed to domestic demand contraction from martial law and global trade shifts, necessitating two supplementary budgets. The ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office (AMRO) forecasts Korea's economic growth at 1.9% and inflation at 2.3% for both this year and next, highlighting increasing burdens from global energy prices despite semiconductor demand and government fiscal support. Experts anticipate the Bank of Korea will likely hold the benchmark interest rate at 2.50% this week but may consider a hike by July due to escalating oil prices and inflation.
sections.Financial Markets: Korean retail investors in overseas stocks ('Seohak Gaemi') are shifting to net selling US equities, influenced by high exchange rates hovering around 1,500 won and stagnant US markets. This trend raises questions about the effectiveness of new domestic market return accounts (RIA) designed to repatriate overseas investment. Bond funds are experiencing significant outflows, with 2.7 trillion won withdrawn in a month, driven by fears of potential US interest rate hikes. Conversely, retail investors are increasingly turning to shorter-term, lower-coupon government bonds as a temporary safe haven from stock market volatility.
sections.Industry & Technology: The recent surge in oil prices is boosting demand for electric vehicles, positively impacting South Korea's three major battery manufacturers—LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI, and SK On—who anticipate improved performance. In response to the energy crisis, the government has reactivated Kori Nuclear Power Plant Unit 2, which had been offline for three years, to enhance energy security. Meanwhile, Japan's EV subsidy policies, which favor domestic batteries, are creating winners like Toyota and challengers like BYD, while also boosting Tesla sales for vehicles using Japanese batteries. LS Electric secured a significant contract to supply ultra-high voltage transformers for a US big tech data center, underscoring growing investment in power infrastructure driven by AI demands.
sections.Real Estate: Financial authorities are implementing stricter lending regulations from April 17, preventing multi-homeowners in the Seoul metropolitan area from extending apartment loan maturities, with an exception for lease contract expirations. Soaring jeonse (lump-sum deposit) prices in Seoul, with transactions reaching 8,759 in March, are driving residents to Gyeonggi Province, subsequently increasing property values there. Looking ahead, April is set to be a busy month for new apartment offerings, with over 2,600 units across 13 complexes nationwide, including the notable Icheon Le El in Yongsan.
sections.International Economy: The US labor market faces significant uncertainty, with some analysts suggesting it is becoming extremely fragile. Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell has indicated he would temporarily assume the role of interim chairman if his designated successor is not confirmed in a timely manner. Key upcoming US economic data, including the March CPI and the revised Q4 GDP, are highly anticipated as they will significantly influence the Federal Reserve's future interest rate decisions. Furthermore, the minutes from the March FOMC meeting are expected, alongside continued market volatility driven by geopolitical tensions, particularly concerning Iran and former President Trump's recent ultimatums.
sections.AI & Economy: The Ministry of Employment and Labor is hosting an APEC forum to discuss the impact of AI on jobs and strategize policy responses, advocating for a shift from 'employment protection' to 'maintaining employability.' Hyundai Motor Group plans a 9 trillion won investment in robotics and AI in Saemangeum, exploring both internal resources and external funds like the National Growth Fund. The escalating demand for AI infrastructure is driving significant investments in power solutions, exemplified by LS Electric's large contract to supply ultra-high voltage transformers for a US data center. Additionally, the optical communication sector is experiencing a surge in stock prices due to its crucial role as a core AI infrastructure component.
sections.Others: GM Korea has achieved significant financial health, reporting over 3 trillion won in net cash last year despite high US tariffs, marking a strong turnaround after three consecutive years of profitability. The Ministry of Economy and Finance is urging immediate execution of supplementary budget funds upon parliamentary approval to provide timely support to citizens affected by the Middle East conflict. Hanmi Pharmaceutical is expanding its new drug development, planning to present the highest number of non-clinical research results among domestic biopharma companies at AACR 2026. Moreover, there is growing interest in senior residences, driven by an aging population and anticipated reforms in property taxes for ultra-high-value and non-resident single-owner homes.
